papers.title: Validation of the BASED Score as a Prognostic Biomarker for Refractory Epilepsy Following Treatment of Infantile Epileptic Spasms Syndrome.
papers.title_zh: 基于婴儿癫痫性痉挛综合征治疗后，验证BASED评分作为难治性癫痫预后生物标志物的有效性。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Refractory epilepsy is common among children with a history of infantile epileptic spasms syndrome (IESS), yet no validated prognostic biomarkers exist to guide early risk stratification. The Burden of Amplitudes and Epileptiform Discharges (BASED) score is an interictal EEG rating scale for children with IESS, with scores of 4 or 5 suggesting epileptic encephalopathy. The objective of this study was to determine whether a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 is a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.
METHODS: This retrospective validation study of children with IESS was conducted at a Level 4 pediatric epilepsy center. Children with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) were excluded. Three blinded reviewers assigned 2021 BASED scores to full-length post-treatment EEGs. Refractory epilepsy was defined as persistent seizures despite treatment with at least 2 antiseizure medications or completion of epilepsy surgery. Prespecified performance benchmarks for BASED 4/5 as a rule-in test required ≥80% specificity and a positive likelihood ratio of ≥4.
RESULTS: The cohort included 123 children (42.3% female), with a median first treatment age of 8.0 months (IQR 5.9-10.3) and follow-up duration after first treatment of 58.8 months (IQR 42.2-80.7). Only 11.4% had a favorable etiology. EEGs (median 19 hours) were completed at a median of 47 days (32-72) after starting treatment. The inter-rater agreement for epileptic encephalopathy was excellent (κfree = 0.78). Half (52%) of the children had refractory epilepsy. BASED 4/5 demonstrated high specificity (88.1%, 95% CI 77.1-95.1) for refractory epilepsy, with a positive likelihood ratio of 4.4 (2.1-9.1). The sensitivity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 51.6% (38.7-64.3), 82.5% (69.3-90.8), and 62.7% (56.1-68.7), respectively. An exploratory composite indicator comprising BASED 4/5, persistent epileptic spasms, and/or epileptic spasms relapse demonstrated higher sensitivity (79.7%, 67.8-88.7) with modestly reduced specificity (81.4%, 69.1-90.3).
DISCUSSION: Study limitations include the single-center design, exclusion of children with TSC, variable EEG timing, and shorter follow-up in some children. Nevertheless, in this independent validation cohort, a post-treatment BASED 4/5 demonstrated favorable prognostic performance consistent with its proposed use as a rule-in test for refractory epilepsy. These findings support a post-treatment BASED score of 4/5 as a prognostic biomarker for refractory epilepsy after IESS treatment.

papers.title: WNK-SPAK/OSR1 signaling pathway facilitates ictal activity via reduced neuronal chloride extrusion rate.
papers.title_zh: WNK-SPAK/OSR1信号通路通过降低神经元氯离子外排速率来促进癫痫发作活动。
papers.abstract: Seizures upregulate Na+-K+-2Cl- (NKCC1)-mediated Cl- influx and downregulate K+-Cl- (KCC2)-mediated Cl- efflux via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 kinases, leading to cytoplasmic chloride ([Cl-]i) accumulation, reduced GABAergic inhibition, and anticonvulsant failure. Early studies found that inhibiting WNK-kinase reduced baseline [Cl-]i (ECl) and seizures via increased KCC2 activity. However, increased KCC2 activity alone should not affect ECl, whose determinants are more complex. We determined the net effects of the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway inhibitor WNK463 on ECl and [Cl-]i transients during spontaneous ictal-like discharges (ILDs) in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures from mice. We found that WNK463 reduced interictal [Cl-]i, but did not change baseline [Cl-]i measured in the presence of TTX. WNK463 enhanced neuronal Cl- extrusion during and after ILDs before abolishing ILDs. Pharmacological inhibition and targeted siRNA silencing demonstrated that the anti-ictal effects of WNK463 involved both NKCC1 and KCC2. Our data support a mechanism whereby mutual NKCC1 inhibition and KCC2 activation via the WNK-SPAK/OSR1 pathway exert powerful anti-ictal effects by facilitating [Cl-]i extrusion during ILDs.

papers.title: Frequency-Specific Thalamocortical Network Dynamics During Focal Seizures in Humans.
papers.title_zh: 人类局灶性癫痫发作期间的频率特异性丘脑皮质网络动力学。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The thalamus is an emerging neuromodulation target in drug-resistant focal epilepsy because of its frequent ictal involvement. However, frequency-specific and directional thalamocortical dynamics remain poorly understood. We sought to characterize thalamocortical network dynamics across seizure evolution using stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG).
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed SEEG recordings from patients with pediatric-onset drug-resistant focal epilepsy with simultaneous cortical and thalamic sampling focusing on the anterior nucleus (AN) and centromedian nucleus (CM). We applied visual analysis with quantitative measures of spectral power, imaginary coherence, and spectral Granger causality across slow (1-12 Hz), β (13-30 Hz), and γ (30-70 Hz) bands to quantify thalamocortical and cortico-cortical interactions from seizure onset to termination. Random forest models were trained to classify seizure state using thalamic EEG features as an exploratory analysis.
RESULTS: The final cohort comprised 19 patients (median age, 16.9 years; 31.6% female), with 66 focal seizures analyzed. Thalamic ictal activity was present at seizure onset in 81% of sampled thalamic contacts and became nearly universal by seizure termination. Both the thalamus and seizure onset zone showed increased spectral power during seizures, with prominent slow-band augmentation at seizure termination in the thalamus. Similarly, thalamocortical imaginary coherence increased during seizures, with the largest changes near seizure termination in the slow band (AN-SOZ: 11% [IQR, 2 to 20], rank-biserial correlations (rrb) = 0.84; CM-SOZ: 12% [IQR, 3 to 23], rrb = 0.84) and β band (AN-SOZ: 5% [IQR, 0 to 12], rrb = 0.74; CM-SOZ: 8% [IQR, 2 to 15], rrb = 0.86). Directed connectivity analyses demonstrated bidirectional thalamocortical interactions, with large slow-frequency thalamus-to-SOZ outflow near seizure termination from both AN and CM, exceeding propagation-zone-to-SOZ cortico-cortical flow (both p < 0.01). Seizure state was classified using thalamic EEG features, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.825 for AN and 0.839 for CM.
DISCUSSION: Human focal seizures engage frequency-specific and bidirectional thalamocortical interactions that evolve from onset to termination. These findings support the thalamus as a source of clinically relevant seizure-state information and may inform thalamic biomarker development for neuromodulation in drug-resistant epilepsy.

papers.title: Real-world safety profiles of newer antiseizure medications: A pharmacovigilance study based on FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database.
papers.title_zh: 新型抗癫痫药物的真实世界安全性特征：一项基于FDA不良事件报告系统数据库的药物警戒研究。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the post-marketing safety of four newer antiseizure medications (ASMs)-brivaracetam (BRV), cannabidiol (CBD), cenobamate (CNB), and fenfluramine (FFA).
METHODS: A pharmacovigilance study was conducted using data from the FAERS database (Q1 2016-Q4 2024). Disproportionality analyses were performed to detect adverse event (AE) signals using three algorithms. Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, reporter, and treatment strategy. We employed multivariable logistic regression, adjusted for covariates including age, sex, weight, dose, and concomitant medications, to validate associations between ASMs and specific AEs and to identify potential influencing factors. Bayesian network analysis was conducted to explore conditional dependencies among variables. Hospitalization risk was evaluated based on system organ classes.
RESULTS: After data cleaning, 13 763 reports were included. We identified 308 positive preferred term (PT) signals. Seizure-related AEs were frequently reported. All four ASMs had the PT of seizure cluster, with each exhibiting distinct AE profiles: BRV with psychiatric disorders, CBD with gastrointestinal events, CNB with visual dysfunction, and FFA with valvular heart disease (VHD). Children had higher reporting odds of seizure with BRV and CBD, while reporting odds of FFA-related VHD were lower in children; polytherapy was associated with higher reporting odds of somnolence, and AE reporting patterns varied by reporter source. Both CBD-related gastrointestinal events and FFA-related cardiac events exhibited dose-dependent effects. Infection-related AEs were associated with higher odds of hospitalization for multiple ASMs.
SIGNIFICANCE: This study comprehensively characterizes the safety profiles of newer ASMs and highlights the importance of tailored AE monitoring based on specific ASM and patient characteristics.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling of the RELN gene using MSP in Iraqi pediatric patients with epilepsy: A case-control study.
papers.title_zh: 使用MSP对伊拉克癫痫儿科患者的RELN基因进行DNA甲基化谱分析：一项病例对照研究。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epilepsy is one of the most common neurological disorders in children and is influenced by both genetic and epigenetic mechanisms. Altered DNA methylation may contribute to disease susceptibility through changes in gene regulation. The RELN gene is involved in neuronal migration, synaptic plasticity, and brain development, making it a potential target for epigenetic investigation.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the association between RELN methylation levels and pediatric epilepsy and to investigate its potential diagnostic value.
METHODS: A case-control study was conducted involving 47 pediatric epilepsy patients and 39 healthy controls. Genomic DNA was extracted and validated prior to methylation analysis. Quantitative real-time PCR using methylation-specific primers was performed to determine RELN methylation percentage. Statistical analyses included Mann-Whitney testing, logistic regression analysis, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, and Spearman correlation analysis.
RESULTS: RELN methylation percentage was significantly higher in patients compared with controls (11.60% [8.88-14.61] vs. 7.77% [6.87-10.73], P < 0.0001). ROC analysis demonstrated good discriminatory performance with an AUC of 0.811 (95% CI: 0.712-0.887), sensitivity of 80.85%, and specificity of 74.36% at a cutoff value > 8.545%. Logistic regression analysis identified RELN methylation as an independent predictor of epilepsy (adjusted OR=1.537, 95% CI: 1.240-1.906, P < 0.001). No significant correlations were observed between RELN methylation and age, age at first seizure, or days since the last seizure.
CONCLUSION: Increased RELN methylation was significantly associated with pediatric epilepsy and independently predicted disease status, suggesting a potential role for RELN methylation as an epigenetic biomarker in epilepsy.

papers.title: Advancing neuropsychological and neurodevelopmental outcome measurement in pediatric epilepsy surgery.
papers.title_zh: 推进小儿癫痫手术中的神经心理和神经发育结局测量。
papers.abstract: Epilepsy surgery is the most effective treatment for appropriately selected children with drug-resistant epilepsy, however, surgical success continues to be defined primarily by seizure outcomes. Neuropsychological and neurodevelopmental outcomes are inconsistently assessed, and children with substantial developmental or neurological impairment may be systematically underrepresented in postoperative outcome data. We conducted an overview of systematic reviews published from 2015 to 2025 that reported outcomes after pediatric epilepsy surgery, with particular emphasis on cognitive, developmental, adaptive, behavioral, and quality-of-life domains. Among 50 eligible systematic reviews, only 22 (44%) reported neuropsychological or cognitive outcomes. Global cognitive measures predominated, whereas language, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed were substantially less frequently assessed. Only nine reviews quantitatively synthesized neurocognitive or developmental outcomes, and substantial heterogeneity in assessment instruments, baseline testing, and postoperative follow-up limited cross-study comparability. These findings highlight the need to move beyond whether neuropsychological testing is performed toward standardized measurement of meaningful longitudinal change. We propose a framework incorporating common core outcome domains, prespecified assessment intervals, developmentally appropriate and floor-sensitive measures, and inclusion of children unable to complete conventional norm-referenced testing. Prospective integration of harmonized neuropsychological trajectories with structural and functional connectomic measures may further clarify how seizure control, surgical network disruption, and neuroplasticity shape postoperative development. Pediatric epilepsy surgery outcomes should therefore encompass both seizure control and preservation or improvement of cognitive, developmental, adaptive, and functional trajectories.

papers.title: Knockdown of KCNQ2 in CA1 reshapes epilepsy-related limbic network rhythms and reduces spontaneous exploratory behavior in mice.
papers.title_zh: 在CA1中敲低KCNQ2可重塑与癫痫相关的边缘系统网络节律，并减少小鼠的自发探索行为。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Circuit-level effects of localized cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily Q member 2 (KCNQ2) loss-of-function on epileptogenesis remain poorly understood, despite the well-established association of KCNQ2 deficiency with epilepsy and neuropsychiatric comorbidities.
METHODS: To examine how CA1-specific KCNQ2 deficiency modulates neural network activity during acquired epileptogenesis, we selectively knocked down KCNQ2 in mouse CA1 via adeno-associated virus (AAV)-short hairpin RNA (shRNA) and explored limbic network alterations. Calcium activity of glutamatergic neurons, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) ergic neurons, somatostatin-positive (SST+) interneurons, and parvalbumin-positive (PV+) interneurons was recorded using cell type-specific GCaMP expression with simultaneous CA1 electroencephalography (EEG). Multi-site EEG recordings from CA1, cornu ammonis 3 (CA3), retrosplenial agranular cortex (RSA), infralimbic cortex (IL), cingulate cortex area 1 (CG1), primary motor cortex (M1), and basolateral amygdala (BLA) were analyzed for spectral power, functional connectivity (FC), and phase-amplitude coupling (PAC). We observed spontaneous activity, novel object recognition, and social behaviors of the model mice.
RESULTS: CA1 KCNQ2 knockdown increased calcium activity in all neuronal populations during the latency, with greater activation of SST+ than PV+ interneurons. Excitatory-inhibitory imbalance correlated with seizure severity. EEG analyses revealed a biphasic pattern: reduced low-frequency power, phase synchrony, and FC during the latency, followed by widespread hypersynchronization of power spectral density, mutual information, and phase synchrony during severe seizures. In the non-epileptic state, PAC analysis revealed that knockdown group developed a biased network configuration characterized by enhanced PAC directed toward the BLA and weakened CA3-M1 and M1-related coupling. This pattern was consistent with their behavioral phenotypes, including reduced central exploration, fewer open-arm entries, impaired novel object exploration, and decreased social preference. During generalized seizures, PAC underwent extensive reorganization, with strengthened coupling between the BLA and multiple brain regions and reduced M1-directed coupling. Intraperitoneally administered retigabine (RTG), a pan-KCNQ channel opener, partially alleviated these behavioral deficits and attenuated the abnormally potentiated long-range network activity.
SIGNIFICANCE: CA1 KCNQ2 knockdown not only disrupts the local excitatory/inhibitory balance but also promotes epileptogenesis by reshaping limbic-cortical network coupling patterns.

papers.title: Antiseizure medication use in self-limited epilepsies of childhood: A scoping review by the ILAE Pediatric Medical Therapies Task Force.
papers.title_zh: 抗癫痫药物在儿童自限性癫痫中的应用：ILAE儿科药物治疗工作组的范围综述。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Self-limited focal epilepsies (SeLFEs) of childhood, including self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), self-limited epilepsy with autonomic seizures (SeLEAS), childhood occipital visual epilepsy (COVE), and photosensitive occipital lobe epilepsy (POLE), are common pediatric epilepsy syndromes with heterogeneous clinical management. We performed a scoping review to synthesize evidence regarding the use, effectiveness, safety, and discontinuation of antiseizure medications (ASMs) in children with SeLFEs.
METHODS: Nine databases were searched from inception to January 2026. Eligible studies included original research reporting ASM-related outcomes in children with SeLFEs. PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses, extension for scoping reviews) guidance was followed.
RESULTS: Sixty-two studies met eligibility criteria, including 11 randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Most studies evaluated SeLECTS (6171 participants), whereas substantially fewer investigated SeLEAS (n = 348), COVE (n = 91), or POLE (n = 26). Evidence was highly heterogeneous and consisted predominantly of retrospective observational studies. In SeLECTS, reported 12-month seizure freedom rates after ASM treatment were approximately 72% across studies, although estimates varied considerably. Evidence for SeLEAS, COVE, and POLE was limited and derived mainly from small retrospective cohorts with heterogeneous methodologies and outcome definitions. Failure of first-line ASM therapy occurred in approximately 30% of patients. Adverse events were reported in approximately 22% of treated children and infrequently led to treatment discontinuation. RCTs generally reported similar seizure outcomes across multiple ASMs, although many trials were limited by small sample sizes and open-label designs.
SIGNIFICANCE: Current evidence suggests that children with SeLFEs often achieve seizure control with ASM treatment and that adverse effects are generally manageable. However, the overall certainty of evidence remains limited because of methodological heterogeneity, predominance of retrospective studies, and limited randomized data. Important evidence gaps remain regarding the need for ASM treatment, optimal treatment duration, and timing of medication withdrawal.

papers.title: Cenobamate in brain tumor-related epilepsy: A multicenter real-world experience.
papers.title_zh: 塞诺巴酯用于治疗脑瘤相关癫痫：一项多中心真实世界经验研究。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Cenobamate (CNB) is a novel antiseizure medication with a dual mechanism of action that has demonstrated high efficacy in drug-resistant focal epilepsy; however, evidence in brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) remains limited. The study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness, safety, and tolerability of CNB as add-on therapy in a multicenter cohort of patients with BTRE.
METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective observational study across tertiary epilepsy centers in the Lazio region, Italy. Adult patients with drug-resistant BTRE treated with CNB as adjunctive therapy were included. Seizure frequency was assessed at baseline and during follow-up. Primary outcomes were changes in monthly seizure frequency and responder rates. Effectiveness was analyzed in both the overall population and in a homogeneous cohort of patients with 6-month follow-up.
RESULTS: Twenty patients (10 females, median age 48 years) were included. Tumor histology included meningioma (n = 7, 35%), astrocytoma (n = 4, 20%), glioblastoma (n = 3, 15%), ganglioglioma (n = 3, 15%), oligodendroglioma (n = 2, 10%), and dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (n = 1, 5%). In the overall analysis population (n = 20), after a median 12-month follow-up, median seizure frequency significantly decreased from 6 to 1 per month (p < 0.001), with a median reduction of 85.8% (IQR 51.4-96.7). Responder rates were 80% (≥50% seizure reduction), 60% (≥75%), and 20% achieved seizure freedom. Adverse events occurred in 12 patients (60%), including sedation (n = 8, 40%), postural instability (n = 3, 15%), diarrhea, and mild cutaneous rash (n = 1, 5% each). CNB was discontinued in one patient (5%).
SIGNIFICANCE: In this multicenter real-world cohort of patients with drug-resistant BTRE and heterogeneous tumor histology, CNB was associated with a reduction in seizure frequency and was well tolerated.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Seizures caused by brain tumors can be difficult to control. We reviewed records from 20 adults who received cenobamate alongside their existing seizure medicines. At their last follow-up, 16 had at least half as many seizures, and four were seizure-free. Twelve patients experienced side effects, most commonly sleepiness; one stopped cenobamate because of a rash. These findings suggest that cenobamate may help some people with brain tumor-related epilepsy. However, the study was small, had no comparison group, and included patients with different tumors and follow-up durations. Larger studies are needed.

papers.title: Invasive monitoring and mapping in epilepsy surgery: Acute and chronic intracranial recording from surface to depth.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫手术中的侵入性监测和定位：从表面到深度的急性和慢性颅内记录。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract: Invasive intracranial recording remains central to the surgical evaluation of drug-resistant focal epilepsy when noninvasive data are insufficient to define the epileptogenic zone or its relationship to eloquent cortex. This review, part of an International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Surgical Therapies Commission education series aligned with the epilepsy surgery curriculum, reviews invasive monitoring and mapping for the practicing and trainee epilepsy surgeon. Consistent with the competency-based ILAE epilepsy surgery curriculum, in which the surgeon is expected to understand and actively contribute to electrode selection, safe implantation, and the interpretation of invasive recordings within the multidisciplinary team, we give particular emphasis to the surgical execution of these methods alongside their electrophysiological rationale. We outline the historical development of the field from intraoperative electrocorticography and subdural recording to stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG), describe acute and chronic recording strategies using both surface and depth approaches, including the operative techniques of implantation and post-implantation electrode localization, and summarize the techniques of functional mapping. We compare subdural and stereotactic methods with respect to coverage, mapping capability, diagnostic yield, seizure outcome, and morbidity, and we review the complication profiles of each. Finally, we discuss future directions, including high-density and chronically implantable probes that combine macro-contacts with microelectrode recording throughout the electrode shaft. We emphasize that the choice of method should follow a clearly stated anatomo-electro-clinical hypothesis, balancing the completeness of sampling against procedural risk.

papers.title: Laser interstitial thermal therapy in older patients with drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy.
papers.title_zh: 激光间质热疗用于治疗药物难治性颞叶内侧癫痫的老年患者。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) is a minimally invasive treatment for focal drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). This study sought to examine the efficacy of LITT for a cohort of older adults with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (MTLE) and evaluate predictors of safety.
METHODS: We examined 24 patients aged ≥50 years, with 10/24 (42%) ≥60 years. Primary outcomes were Engel classification and reduction from baseline seizure frequency. We additionally reviewed post-ablation complications, hospital length of stay (LOS), neurocognitive and psychiatric worsening, and anti-seizure medication (ASM) reduction. The Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) was calculated to assess its utility in prediction of postoperative complications.
RESULTS: 22/24 (92%) had ≥50% reduction in seizure frequency, and 17/24 (71%) had ≥90% reduction at last follow-up, with median follow-up of 5.2 years (range, 1.5-10.4 years). Engel Class I outcome was achieved in 19/24 (79%) of patients by 6 months post-ablation and maintained in 12/24 (50%) of patients by last follow-up. Immediate postoperative complications were mostly transient, though worse cognitive symptoms were reported in 5/24 (21%), and worse mood was reported in 3/24 (13%) at 6 months post-ablation. Higher CCI did not correlate with complications but was associated with prolonged LOS. ASM reduction occurred in half of patients.
SIGNIFICANCE: In our cohort, LITT offered favorable seizure and safety outcomes in an older population with focal DRE. Perioperative risk assessments such as the CCI may be useful in older patient selection for LITT.

papers.title: Preoperative hippocampal volume, resection extent, and 5-year stability of seizure freedom after temporal lobe epilepsy surgery.
papers.title_zh: 颞叶癫痫手术后的术前海马体积、切除范围和5年无癫痫发作的稳定性。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether preoperative ipsilateral hippocampal volume modifies the association between hippocampal resection extent and durable 5-year seizure freedom after temporal lobe epilepsy surgery.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective secondary analysis of the public Imaging Database for Epilepsy And Surgery. Patients undergoing temporal lobectomy or temporal lesionectomy were eligible. The exposure was ipsilateral hippocampal resection fraction, the modifier was preoperative ipsilateral hippocampal volume z-score, and the outcome was International League Against Epilepsy class 1 at every annual assessment from years 1 through 5. Multivariable logistic regression included their interaction and pathology, procedure type, preoperative focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures, age, epilepsy duration, antiseizure medication count, sex, and operative side.
RESULTS: Among 353 patients undergoing temporal surgery, 220 had all five annual outcomes and 210 had complete primary-model data. Durable seizure freedom occurred in 82 of 210 patients (39.0%). The resection-by-volume interaction odds ratio was 1.49 (95% confidence interval, 1.01-2.21; p = .045). Model-based probabilities increased with greater resection when hippocampal volume was preserved but not with marked atrophy. The estimate was similar in temporal lobectomy alone (odds ratio, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.07-2.83) and attenuated after inverse-probability weighting (odds ratio, 1.43; 95% confidence interval, .95-2.13).
SIGNIFICANCE: In this cohort, the association between measured hippocampal resection overlap and seizure outcome varied across preoperative hippocampal volumes. The pattern was most apparent when seizure freedom was assessed across 5 years rather than at a single postoperative visit.

papers.title: Real-world antiseizure medication prescribing and treatment pathways in a pediatric health care system.
papers.title_zh: 儿科医疗保健系统中抗癫痫药物的真实世界处方和治疗途径。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize antiseizure medication (ASM) selection, subsequent ASM prescribing, and treatment pathways among patients with epilepsy receiving care within a pediatric health care system.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective electronic health record study over 17 years. Each unique ASM was counted once per patient, and ASMs were ordered by the date of their first observed prescription. For each observed ASM, we determined whether a subsequent unique ASM was prescribed during available follow-up. Prescription of a third unique ASM was used as a proxy for potential drug-resistant epilepsy.
RESULTS: Among 20 009 patients, 27 ASMs and 3507 treatment pathways were identified. The most common first-observed ASMs were levetiracetam (35.1%), oxcarbazepine (17.2%), and valproic acid (12.3%). From 2010 to 2026, the proportion of first-observed prescriptions for levetiracetam increased from 23.1% to 41.5%. The proportion of all distinct ASMs first recorded for individual patients that were newer-generation ASMs increased from 0% in 2010 to 9.1% in 2026. The proportion of patients without a subsequent ASM ranged from 16.2% to 69.6% across commonly prescribed first-observed ASMs. Overall, 55.6% of patients had one unique ASM recorded, 22.4% had two, and 22.0% had at least three, thereby meeting the study's prescription-based proxy for potential drug-resistant epilepsy. Beyond the most common single- and two-ASM pathways, each remaining pathway accounted for less than 1% of the cohort.
SIGNIFICANCE: Prescribing remained concentrated among established ASMs, although their relative use changed substantially. The proportion of patients without a subsequent ASM varied widely across medications, and treatment pathways beyond first-observed therapy were highly heterogeneous. These findings characterize real-world treatment patterns and identify a need for comparative effectiveness studies of ASM sequencing.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: We examined antiseizure medication prescribing over 17 years among more than 20 000 patients with epilepsy receiving care in a pediatric health care system. More than half had only one medication recorded, whereas 22% had at least three medications; however, the available records could not determine whether these medications failed to control seizures. Levetiracetam became more commonly prescribed, newer medications remained a small proportion of overall use, and medication sequences varied widely after the first observed treatment. These findings highlight the need for better evidence to guide medication selection after initial treatment.

papers.title: Etiology and geographic variation in acute symptomatic seizure management: An international vignette-based survey.
papers.title_zh: 急性症状性癫痫发作管理的病因和地域差异：一项基于案例的国际调查。
authors: International League Against Epilepsy Acute Symptomatic Seizure Task Force
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute symptomatic seizures (ASyS) account for nearly half of new onset seizures, but evidence guiding management remains limited. We aimed to characterize international variation in ASyS management across common etiologies.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, vignette-based survey through the International League Against Epilepsy national chapters (February to May 2025). Five etiology-based vignettes assessed clinical and electrographic ASyS scenario after ischemic stroke, traumatic brain injury (TBI), meningitis, hyponatremia, and alcohol withdrawal. Respondents who managed neonatal seizures completed a neonatal stroke vignette. We assessed antiseizure medication (ASM) initiation, duration after clinical ASyS, and continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) use. Interrespondent variability was quantified by normalized Shannon entropy (H'). Multivariable generalized estimating equations accounted for repeated responses.
RESULTS: Among 963 respondents (92 countries), 62% recommended ASM initiation in clinical and 61% in electrographic ASyS scenarios. Overall ASM initiation variability was high (H' = .96), highest for alcohol withdrawal (H' = 1.0), followed by stroke (H' > .9), and consistently higher for electrographic than clinical ASyS. Etiology was the strongest driver of ASM initiation. Compared with stroke, ASM initiation odds were higher for TBI (odds ratio [OR] = 2.5, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 2.2-2.8) and meningitis (OR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.7-2.2), and lower for hyponatremia (OR = .2, 95% CI = .2-.2) and alcohol withdrawal (OR = .5, 95% CI = .5-.6). Compared with Europe, initiation odds were higher in North America (OR = 2.7, 95% CI = 2.0-3.6), Asia-Oceania (OR = 2.4, 95% CI = 2.0-3.0), and Latin America (OR = 2.0, 95% CI = 1.5-2.7), but not Africa. These differences persisted after accounting for country income. Compared with stroke, the mean ASM duration was 3.2 months shorter for hyponatremia and .6 months longer for TBI. Alcohol withdrawal durations were polarized (41% discontinued at discharge; 20% continued >12 months). cEEG use was markedly higher in North America than Europe (OR = 11.3, 95% CI = 7.8-16.5). Among 291 neonatal respondents, 75% continued ASM beyond discharge.
SIGNIFICANCE: ASyS management varies markedly, reaching near-maximal heterogeneity in several common scenarios. Although etiology drives decisions, geography and provider characteristics also influence care, underscoring an urgent need for randomized trials and international consensus guidance to harmonize care.

papers.title: Ketogenic diet therapy in adolescents and adults with epilepsy: A scoping review of cognitive outcomes.
papers.title_zh: 癫痫青少年和成年患者的生酮饮食疗法：对认知结局的范围综述。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The ketogenic diet treatment (KDT) is an established non-pharmacological treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, rigorous research for seizure efficacy based on randomized controlled studies in adolescents and adults remains limited, and cognitive outcomes are rarely assessed using standardized measures.
METHODS: This scoping review has mapped evidence on cognitive outcomes of KDT in adolescents and adults with epilepsy. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched for studies published between 1986 and 2026. Eligibility for this review required inclusion of adolescents or adults with epilepsy receiving KDT and reporting cognitive outcomes.
RESULTS: Of 951 records, 19 studies were included. Overall, KDT was associated with favorable seizure and cognitive outcomes, although reports of cognitive outcomes were generally subjective.
SIGNIFICANCE: Rigorous research designs were scarce, and evidence remains limited; future studies should use stronger designs, larger samples, standardized cognitive assessments, and longer follow-up periods.
PLAIN LANGUAGE SUMMARY: Research shows that people with epilepsy often experience difficulties with the brain's ability to process information. While dietary treatments have been shown to be effective for seizure control, less is known about their effects on cognition. We reviewed published research examining cognitive outcomes in adolescents and adults with epilepsy following dietary treatment. Most studies suggested that these diets had a positive effect on aspects of cognitive functioning. However, the available evidence remains limited. More studies with better designs using well-established cognitive assessments are needed to better understand these effects.

papers.title: Scalp high-frequency oscillations differentiate neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy with and without electroencephalographically confirmed seizures.
papers.title_zh: 头皮高频振荡可区分患有缺氧缺血性脑病的新生儿，无论其是否经脑电图证实存在癫痫发作。
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) is a leading cause of neonatal seizures, but seizure detection is challenging when continuous electroencephalography (EEG) is unavailable and neonates undergo only a single routine EEG. Biomarkers derived from routine EEG may aid identification of neonates with seizures. We investigated whether scalp high-frequency oscillation (HFO) rates derived from the first eligible routine EEG (1) differentiate neonates with HIE with and without seizures; and (2) contribute to seizure classification alongside established clinical, neurophysiological, and imaging biomarkers.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed routine scalp EEG recordings from 33 term neonates with HIE (17 with seizures, 16 without), obtained at a mean postnatal age of 4 ± 3 days. The mean analyzed EEG duration was 38 ± 14 min in neonates with seizures and 36 ± 20 min in those without. HFO rates in sleep segments were quantified using a validated automated detector.
RESULTS: Scalp HFO rates were significantly higher in neonates with seizures than in those without (.12 ± .11 vs. .03 ± .02 HFOs/min/channel, adjusted p = .02). An HFO rate threshold of .07 HFOs/min/channel optimally discriminated neonates who had seizures from those who did not (area under the curve [AUC] = .81). HFO rates did not differ significantly according to HIE severity, therapeutic hypothermia, antiseizure medication response, EEG background activity, or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) abnormalities. Multivariable models incorporating HFO rate, EEG background activity, and MRI findings showed discrimination (AUC = .92, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .69-1.00 for logistic regression; AUC = 1.00, 95% CI = .75-1.00 for random forest), with HFO rate as the strongest contributor to seizure classification.
SIGNIFICANCE: These findings support scalp HFO rate as a potential electrophysiological biomarker of seizure occurrence in neonatal HIE, complementary to EEG background assessment and MRI findings. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether HFOs can predict subsequent seizures.

papers.title: Strengths and weaknesses in epilepsy training across residency programs in Italy: A multicenter survey by the Italian chapter of the Young Epilepsy Section (YES-I).
papers.title_zh: 意大利住院医师培训项目癫痫培训的优势和不足：意大利青年癫痫分会（YES-I）的多中心调查。
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study was to assess epilepsy-related services across Italian neurology and child neuropsychiatry residency programs, evaluate residents and early-career specialists' perceived strengths/weaknesses in epilepsy training, and identify unmet needs and expectations for improving residency programs and Young Epilepsy Section (YES)-Italy educational initiatives.
METHODS: A nationwide cross-sectional survey was conducted between January and April 2026 by a focus group of the YES-Italy Education Task Force. A structured questionnaire was distributed to neurology and child neuropsychiatry residents and specialists within 2 years of completing residency, assessing demographics, epilepsy-related services, self-perceived competencies, training strengths and limitations, and suggestions for improving residency curricula with YES-Italy educational activities. Descriptive statistics were used; group comparisons (neurology vs. child neuropsychiatry; residents vs. early-career specialists) employed the Mann-Whitney U test.
RESULTS: The survey was completed by 150 participants. Epilepsy training was widely available (85.3%) but variable and often brief (<6 months). EEG training was mostly embedded within epilepsy rotation (32.7%), organized as a distinct brief rotation (<3 months; 33.3%), or not available (19.3%). Core epilepsy services were widely present (inpatient wards 82.7%; neurophysiology laboratories 93.3%), while other services were less common (such as epilepsy surgery). Marked variability in Status Epilepticus management emerged across centers. Participants perceived adequate competence for core clinical-diagnostic domains, but lower competence for EEG interpretation and complementary disciplines. Perceived competence was higher in chronic than in acute care. Child neuropsychiatrists reported greater competence in neuropsychology and genetics, neurologists in neuroimaging and acute management. Clinical rotations and multidisciplinary case discussions were major strengths, whereas lectures and direct teaching required improvement. Suggestions for the YES-I group highlighted improving EEG training, structured educational initiatives, access to courses, webinars, and scientific materials.
SIGNIFICANCE: This survey highlights substantial heterogeneity and weaknesses in Italian epilepsy training, particularly regarding EEG interpretation, complementary diagnostics, and acute management, underscoring the need for national standardization, multidisciplinary educational pathways, and strengthened educational initiatives.

papers.title: Dopamine D2 receptor signaling alleviates seizure-related neuronal ferroptosis via MARCH8-mediated P2RX7 ubiquitination.
papers.title_zh: 多巴胺D2受体信号传导通过MARCH8介导的P2RX7泛素化减轻癫痫相关的神经元铁死亡。
papers.abstract: Epilepsy affects over 70 million people worldwide and remains a major cause of morbidity and premature death. Although dopaminergic signaling dysfunction has been implicated in this disorder, its protective mechanisms are not fully understood. Here, we demonstrated that dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression is downregulated during seizures and that D2R signaling protects against seizure. We identified the purinergic receptor P2RX7-a known mediator of neuronal injury - as a downstream target of D2R. Activation of D2R signaling alleviated P2RX7-dependent neuronal ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of cell death, and attenuated seizure-related neuronal injury by promoting ubiquitination and degradation of P2RX7. Mechanistically, D2R signaling upregulated the E3 ubiquitin ligase MARCH8 in an AMPK-dependent manner. MARCH8 promoted K48-linked polyubiquitination of P2RX7, thereby targeting it for proteasomal degradation in neurons. The protective effect of D2R was attenuated in March8 knockout mice, supporting the involvement of MARCH8 in this pathway. Together, our findings identify a neuroprotective mechanism wherein D2R signaling promotes MARCH8-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of P2RX7, alleviating seizure-related neuronal ferroptosis. This work provides new insights into the pathogenesis of seizure-related neuronal injury and identifies potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: From Variability to Synchrony: Non-linear Development of Auditory Neural Responses During the First Year of Life.
papers.title_zh: 从变异性到同步性：生命第一年听觉神经反应的非线性发育。
papers.abstract: In humans, the first year of life is characterized by rapid developmental changes, including substantial brain maturation. As a result, neural responses to auditory stimuli undergo marked changes during this period. In this study, we followed 69 infants across their first year of life and recorded high-density electroencephalography (hdEEG) at 2 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum. Infants were presented with pure beep tones to examine the development of neural responses to auditory stimulation. We analyzed event-related potentials (ERPs), inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC), and event-related spectral perturbation (ERSP) responses to the beep tones and controlled for arousal state during stimulus presentation. We found that with increasing age, neural responses became more pronounced and showed reduced trial-to-trial variability. Phase synchronization increased from 2 weeks to later developmental stages in a broad low-frequency range (0.5 Hz to 13.6 Hz), indicating improved temporal alignment of brain responses over time. However, phase synchronization decreased from 6 to 12 months, suggesting a developmental transition towards more differentiated brain activity. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that auditory maturation during the first year of life follows a non-linear trajectory driven by dynamic changes in neural synchronization, reflecting the progressive refinement of functional neural circuits. Our results thus provide a critical benchmark for understanding the neural dynamics underlying sensory development during this period.

papers.title: From features to digital biomarkers: EEG-fNIRS classification pipelines for brain monitoring.
papers.title_zh: 从特征到数字生物标志物：用于脑监测的EEG-fNIRS分类流程。
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. This review provides a structured overview of EEG- and fNIRS-based classification studies, with a particular focus on signal processing workflows and biomarker extraction. The reviewed literature is organized around key stages of the analytical pipeline, including target formulation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Common feature families-spanning spectral, temporal, connectivity-based, network-level, and hemodynamic representations-are summarized and discussed in relation to their typical applications and limitations. The main contribution is an evidence-based distinction between signal features and credible candidate biomarkers. Reliability, analytical robustness, external generalization, and interpretability are considered within the intended context of use. Clinical utility is assessed separately from predictive performance. Across 117 primary studies, most measures remained candidate biomarkers; only four studies were assigned to independent clinical validation, with qualifications, and none evaluated clinical utility.

papers.title: Globus Pallidus Externus α-Band Activity Decreases After Deep Brain Stimulation in Clinically Responsive Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Patients.
papers.title_zh: 在临床上对强迫症患者进行深部脑刺激后，苍白球外侧部的α波段活动降低。
papers.journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior limb of the internal capsule (ALIC) is an effective treatment for severe obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Identifying brain readouts of a positive response may guide further DBS optimization.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We measured local field potential (LFP) changes from bilateral DBS leads in ten patients with OCD who were implanted at a uniform tractographic network target derived from prior DBS responders. We consistently stimulated dorsal lead contacts in the ALIC white matter while recording LFP from the ventral lead contacts in the grey matter of the anterior globus pallidus externus (GPe), a key node in the basal ganglia nonmotor indirect pathway.
RESULTS: After six months of DBS, OCD symptoms decreased by 40% on average across patients, along with a significant decrease in α-activity across both hemispheres. Only one patient did not have an improvement in symptoms, and this was also the only patient who never exhibited a decrease in α in either hemisphere.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that therapeutic ALIC DBS coincides with a stable decrease in limbic-cognitive GPe α-power, which should be further investigated as a potential biomarker of sustained response.

papers.title: An Implantable In-Tube System for Quantitative Precision Vagus Neuromodulation and Feedback of Intestinal Motility.
papers.title_zh: 一种用于定量精准迷走神经神经调节和肠蠕动反馈的可植入管内系统。
papers.abstract: Electrical vagus neuromodulation of intestinal motility has demonstrated significant clinical utility in the field, where targeting the brain-gut axis can serve as an adjunct in treating intestinal diseases. However, quantitatively understanding vagus-intestine interoceptive information about real-time and in situ feedback on intestinal motility under the influence of electrical stimulation parameters is one of the most urgent challenges. Here we propose an implantable closed-loop system that combines a scalable catheter-type ionic piezoelectric (in-tube) sensor as diverse as the gut, a microelectronic chip, an electrical vagus stimulation electrode, and a display interface to realize point-of-care precision vagus neuromodulation and feedback of intestinal motility. Owing to the radial gradient hydrogel structure design and stress concentration effect, the in-tube sensor can simultaneously quantitatively detect and display four key parameters of intestinal motility, including intensity, frequency, duration, and local compression rate, with a high sensitivity of 7.0 mV mmHg-1 and unique pressure-time integral behavior with a time sensitivity of 24.1 mV s-1, making up for the deficiency of traditional sensors that cannot obtain pressure duration. After implanting the in-tube sensor in the anatomically challenging intestinal lumen of rabbits, we intuitively show how electrical vagus stimulation affects intestinal motility, which guides the optimal frequency window of 5 ∼ 10 Hz.

papers.title: Toward Closed-Loop Cognitive Modulation in Alzheimer's Disease: BCI-Relevant Evidence and a Translational Roadmap.
papers.title_zh: 迈向阿尔茨海默病闭环认知调节：与脑机接口相关的证据和转化路线图。
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) has entered a biomarker-defined era, yet most cognitive and neuromodulatory interventions continue to use fixed targets, timing, and doses. This targeted narrative review maps brain-computer interface (BCI) and closed-loop-relevant evidence in AD and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) by examining how sensing, control, and intervention modules are used prospectively. Read modules include electroencephalography (EEG), functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), real-time functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), functional ultrasound (fUS) and transcranial ultrasound localization microscopy (t-ULM), and digital measures. Control functions include feature extraction, within-person state decoding, uncertainty-aware decision rules, target-engagement assessment, and safety oversight. Write modules include neurofeedback, sensory gamma and sleep-phase acoustic stimulation, transcranial alternating-current stimulation (tACS), transcranial direct-current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), transcranial pulse stimulation (TPS), transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS), transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM), and focused ultrasound-mediated blood-brain barrier (FUS-BBB) opening. Human studies have separately demonstrated signal-contingent feedback, individualized targeting, physiological target engagement, home delivery, and emerging sensing, while preclinical studies provide mechanistic support for gamma, optical, and ultrasound approaches. Sleep-phase acoustic stimulation additionally demonstrates early automated signal-to-stimulus control. Passive sensing provides observations, personalization sets baseline parameters, state-informed control uses current signals to alter delivery, and target engagement verifies the proximal response without establishing clinical efficacy. Reliable decoding of waking cognitive states, broader controller utility, and durable clinical benefit remain unvalidated. We therefore organize the field around disease context, state sensing, feature extraction, state decoding, bounded decision/intervention, response verification, and safety oversight. The decisive early design compares assignments to an adaptive policy with otherwise matched fixed delivery; a sham arm can additionally test intervention efficacy. Such trials must prespecify decoder calibration, uncertainty, abstention, safety limits, and mechanistic and clinical endpoints. Closed-loop cognitive modulation therefore defines a translational research agenda for AD.

papers.title: Bridging the autonomic divide: Closed-loop spinal cord stimulation as a dynamic therapy for parkinsonian orthostatic hypotension.
papers.title_zh: 弥合自主神经系统分歧：闭环脊髓刺激作为帕金森氏病性体位性低血压的动态疗法。
papers.abstract: Neurogenic orthostatic hypotension (nOH) in Parkinson's disease (PD) represents a potential "central-peripheral disconnection" rather than an isolated peripheral deficit. Driven by progressive sympathetic denervation, this uncoupling leaves the peripheral effectors in a fragile, "sick-but-not-dead" state, while simultaneously exposing the central nervous system (CNS) to recurrent hypoperfusion and aberrant central network reorganization. Current static pharmacological therapies fail to accommodate dynamic postural demands, frequently exacerbate supine hypertension (SH), and impose continuous metabolic strain on already compromised peripheral nerves. We hypothesized that closed-loop spinal cord stimulation (SCS) may emerge as a dynamic neuroprosthetic bridge. By providing posture-responsive subthreshold facilitation to residual sympathetic nerves, closed-loop SCS may restore orthostatic hemodynamics without exacerbating SH. This intermittent, on-demand stimulation theoretically provides essential "metabolic unloading" to vulnerable peripheral fibers, avoiding the continuous overdrive inherent to static therapies. Concurrently, by stabilizing systemic blood pressure, it has the potential to act as a hemodynamic shield, protecting the already vulnerable brain from the secondary ischemic hits that may contribute to cognitive decline. To bridge the translational gap between experimental physiology and clinical deployment, we propose a multidimensional candidacy matrix, incorporating hemodynamic, morphological, and functional reserve testing, to systematically identify optimal candidates for this intervention. By stabilizing peripheral hemodynamics and alleviating the allostatic burden on central networks, closed-loop SCS may transcend static symptomatic relief, offering a comprehensive strategy for dynamic physiological restoration and systemic neuroprotection.

papers.title: Medicare Claims-Identified Functional Neurosurgery Workforce in the United States: National Trends, Geographic Distribution, and Access.
papers.title_zh: 美国医疗保险索赔中确定的功能神经外科从业人员：全国趋势、地域分布和可及性。
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The national distribution and geographic accessibility of the functional neurosurgery workforce remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated longitudinal trends in the claims-identified workforce and Medicare-billed service volume, geographic distribution, and county-level proximity to functional neurosurgical care in the United States.
METHODS: Medicare Physician and Other Practitioners data were analyzed from 2013 through 2024. Core functional neurosurgeons were identified as neurosurgery specialists with reportable Medicare fee-for-service (FFS) billing for selected deep brain stimulation, MR-guided focused ultrasound, responsive neurostimulation, Vagus nerve stimulation, or stereoelectroencephalography services. Annual provider and service counts were normalized to Original Medicare FFS beneficiary person-years. For 2024, straight-line distance from each county internal point to the nearest identified provider was calculated, weighted by county population, and evaluated by Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and rurality.
RESULTS: Claims-identified providers increased from 142 in 2013 to 189 in 2024, while Medicare-billed services increased from 6,311 to 7,702. After FFS normalization, provider and service rates increased by 47.6% and 35.4%, respectively. Among 3,109 counties, the equal-county median distance was 72.9 miles (IQR, 43.3-113.7); 30.8% were more than 100 miles away and 7.1% were more than 200 miles away. The population-weighted median was 26.8 miles (IQR, 10.0-59.6), with 10.0% and 2.3% of the population residing in counties more than 100 and 200 miles away, respectively. After adjustment for rurality, SVI was not independently associated with continuous distance.
CONCLUSIONS: Medicare FFS-observable provider and billing activity increased between 2013 and 2024, while substantial county-level geographic disparities were observed in 2024. Workforce planning should consider geographic distribution, rural access, referral networks, and longitudinal multidisciplinary care.

papers.title: The mammalian regulatory architecture: biobehavioral portals and the organization of physiological state.
papers.title_zh: 哺乳动物的调节结构：生物行为门户和生理状态的组织。
papers.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulatory interventions can produce overlapping adaptive outcomes despite engaging substantially different biological pathways. Pathway-centered approaches identify how interventions initially engage the nervous system and characterize pathway-specific mechanisms. Convergence across interventions raises an additional question: how can different biological routes influence overlapping domains of adaptive function?
METHODS: This conceptual paper develops the Mammalian Regulatory Architecture (MRA), an organizational framework informed by identified mammalian synapomorphies (shared derived characteristics) and comparative anatomical, developmental, physiological, and functional observations.
RESULTS: The MRA hypothesizes that mammalian evolution reorganized relationships among conserved regulatory processes through their integration with mammalian specializations and regulatory demands associated with nursing, prolonged developmental dependency, caregiving, co-regulation, and reciprocal social communication. The framework provides the basis for a biological portal model of neuromodulation that distinguishes the pathway of initial engagement from the functional significance of that engagement within the broader regulatory architecture. Whereas the pathway identifies how an intervention initially engages the nervous system, its portal significance concerns how that engagement influences state-regulating processes within the MRA.
DISCUSSION: The proposed framework reframes neuromodulation from a process defined primarily by its neural target or pathway to one in which pathway engagement may influence broader regulatory organization, physiological state, Accessibility-the state-dependent availability of existing adaptive capacities-and adaptive function. It offers an organizational account of how distinct biological routes may influence overlapping domains of adaptive function.
